answer: Each agent can earn influence only by completing tasks that counterparties later verify, with rewards released after a delay and disputes settled from a bond posted upfront. A grove of new identities therefore cannot gain weight just by appearing: each must lock scarce collateral and build a history across independent partners. The pulse of verified work raises trust gradually, while a terrace of linked accounts risks losing its bonds together if collusion is proven. The attacker pays capital and time, and can still be slashed.
